packageRules.description: Runtime dependencies ship in the published wheel, so their bumps should cut a release. Everything else Renovate touches (dev groups, GitHub Actions, the uv build stage) defaults to a non-releasable 'chore'.

The runtime base image ships in the published container, which is built only on release tags — so a base-image bump must cut a release to reach the published image. The uv builder stage is build-only and stays a non-releasable 'chore'.

ghcr.io exposes no release timestamps to Renovate, so under the default 'timestamp-required' behaviour this image's updates are held forever and the 7-day gate can never pass. Let this one digest-pinned, first-party image through without a timestamp (the 7-day age still applies whenever a timestamp is available); every other dependency still requires one.
One uv release fans out into three updates (the builder image tag, the 'astral-sh/uv' version pinned in workflows, and the setup-uv action). Ship them as one PR.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Renovate's pep621 manager only re-locks when a pyproject.toml constraint changes, so versions that already satisfy our ranges (transitive deps especially) freeze in uv.lock between constraint bumps. Lock file maintenance runs a periodic full re-resolve (the automated equivalent of 'uv lock --upgrade') and opens a PR, gated by the existing 'uv lock --check' + pytest matrix. The runtime image is built with 'uv sync --frozen', so uv.lock is exactly what ships in the published container — like a base-image bump, a lock refresh must cut a release to reach it, so these updates are a releasable 'deps'. Renovate has no release timestamp for a full re-lock, so its minimumReleaseAge gate could never pass here; the age is instead enforced by uv itself via [tool.uv] exclude-newer in pyproject.toml, which applies to every transitive package in the re-resolve (and to sync-lock and local 'uv lock' runs too).
